Siddharth Prakash <siddharth.prakash10@gmail.com>:
Dear Sir/Madam,We plan to use Avicenna app for cycling data collection for a PhD study. This will involve using the features GPS, Activity recognition and Bluetooth beacon features in the app. Could you please let us know the features available in trial version and the full license version ? Please also let us know the pricing for the full licensed version. Regards, Siddharth------

Amin Ghaffari:
Sara Farnya Please respond. I believe I need to learn how our pricing works to be able to get back to such cases.------

Sara Farnya:
Amin Ghaffari Sure. However, please feel free to just move them to the "Sales" group, as they don't belong in the "Support" group. Thank you.------

Amin Ghaffari:
Sara Farnya sure will do.------

Mohammad Hashemian:
Maryam Hashemian Can you take care of this ticket today? Thanks. Just get back to them and explain how our Trial & License studies are different and how our pricing works.------

Maryam Hashemian:
Mohammad HashemianSure.------

Maryam Hashemian:
Mohammad HashemianHi Siddharth.I hope you are doing well.This is Maryam from the Avicenna Research team and I would be happy to assist you with any questions you may have.We built Avicenna to help researchers and clinicians automate their research work including field deployment, data collection, and monitoring. I’ve created a slide deck highlighting some of our product's features.To answer your question, the trial version of Avicenna comes with no limitation on creating a study or using the features. You can simply create a study and add any activities that you would like to your study in order to explore how everything works. However, in order to provide a better service for licensed studies, the collected data gets deleted every 30 days but the body of the study and enrolled participants stay intact. Also, we offer an Annual Subscription License, which allows for an unlimited number of projects to be conducted. To be more clear, by Avicenna subscription license you can run as many projects as you like as long as you don't exceed your license quota.Regarding your inquiry about the pricing, it depends on three factors: The type of data you plan to collect (only surveys and experience sampling, or sensor data as well) The participation period (how long each participant will be enrolled in your study) The maximum number of participants you expect to enroll Our pricing unit is called participant/week or P/W for short. Each P/W represents the data you can collect from 1 participant during 1 week. For example, 100 P/W means you collect data from 100 participants for 1 week. Now you can use this in any combination that you want. For example, instead of 100 participants for 1 week, you can conduct 2 studies each with 50 participants and 1 week, as the total again would be 100 P/W.If you share more information about your study (the three factors that I mentioned above), I will be able to provide you with a quote very quickly.If you need any further clarification, don't hesitate to contact me.Best,Maryam------
